rules.title: Limit on upfront charges by lessors (no application fees)
rules.requirement: Before a tenancy begins, a lessor may require payment only of first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit, and a lock-change fee. Application, pet, cleaning, amenity and all other upfront charges by landlords are forbidden. Per the source's legal opinion, landlords also should not require applicants to pay a third-party screening service.
rules.key_value: Only first month's rent, last month's rent, security deposit and lock-change fee allowed; no application fee by lessor
rules.exemptions: Licensed brokers (a separate bona fide business) may charge fees to prospective tenants under broker rules; a landlord who is also a broker likely may not.
rules.interaction: Broker fees are governed separately by 254 CMR 7 and G.L. c.112 § 87DDD1/2.
rules.quoted_span: It states that prior to the beginning of a tenancy, no lessor may require payment for anything except first, last, security, and locks
rules.penalty: In Perry v. Equity Residential Management (2014), the court awarded tenants treble damages and attorney's fees for unlawful upfront application fees.

rules.title: Broker fee written disclosure requirements
rules.requirement: A licensed broker charging a fee to a prospective tenant must, at the first personal meeting, give the applicant written notice of the amount of the fee, the time and manner of payment, and whether the fee is contingent on the owner and applicant entering into a lease or rental agreement. The applicant must sign the notice; if the applicant refuses, the broker must record the refusal on the notice.
rules.key_value: Written broker fee disclosure required at first personal meeting
rules.interaction: Brokers may charge fees that lessors are barred from charging under G.L. c.186 § 15B.
rules.quoted_span: In addition to holding a valid license, the broker has to tell the applicant in writing the amount of the broker’s fee, the time and manner of payment, and whether it is contingent on the owner and applicant actually entering into a lease or rental agreement.

rules.title: Only licensed brokers may charge fees for finding rental housing
rules.requirement: No person may engage in the business of finding dwelling accommodations for prospective tenants for a fee unless that person is a licensed broker or salesman.
rules.key_value: Fee for apartment-finding only by licensed broker or salesman
rules.quoted_span: no person shall engage in the business of finding dwelling accommodations for prospective tenants for a fee unless such person is a licensed broker or salesman.
